Homophones are words that are pronounced the same but differ in meaning or spelling. In other words, homophones are classified as words with two spellings and two meanings, but only one pronunciation.
Here, wine is the drink and whine is the verb meaning to complain. They have different spellings and meanings but you say them exactly the same way.

Homonyms are words that are spelled and pronounced the same but have different meanings. In other words, homonyms are words with one spelling and one pronunciation, but two unrelated meanings, such as while (adverb) and while (verb).
Let's have a glass of wine.
Maybe while we're waiting I could play you the radio ad for the book.
That will help while away the time.

You can report what people say or think using an noun in the reporting clause followed by reported that, to-infinitive or a wh-clause.

The claim is often made that eating too much sugar causes diabetes.
The boss carried out his threat to fire anyone who failed to meet the deadline.
Jessica raised the question of how many new people could reasonably be trained.

images.text:
Adam: Well, I think we're all set. We still have an hour before the guests show up. Let's have a glass of wine. Come on. Please?
Kristi: Adam, don't whine. We'll have a glass after it's all done. Maybe while we're waiting I could play you the radio ad for the book. That will help while away the time.
Adam: Okay. Do you have it on your laptop?
Kristi: Yes. Just let me set up my speakers. Okay. Here it is.

Radio Announcer: Did you hear? Social media is here to stay! Twitter, instagram, snapchat, facebook. Kids and media. If it's out there, they're on it. Do you know what they are reading? Do you know what they are seeing? Do you know who they are talking to? Facebook makes the claim that kids under 13 are not allowed on facebook but there's no way for facebook to verify a user's age? You probably don't know how to protect your kids from the dangers of using social media. Well, now there's a little book that will enable you to protect your kids the way you want to. Marisa Mitchell gives an explanation that will open your eyes to the world of social media. Winnie's World is a book written for kids and parents. Join Winnie as she explores the different types of social media and learns what is safe and what is not. This book makes a promise to spark open conversation between parents and kids so that everyone feels safe and secure.

Adam: Wow. It's a little intense. Does it have to be so scary?
Kristi: That's what I thought. The advertiser made the decision that we needed to catch parents' attention that way, but I'm not sure I agree. Marisa raised the question of its appropriateness so I think we need to make some changes. This is just a draft. We don't need to release the ad until next week for the book release date.
